evidence.label: The tanker fill hose end was submerged in the tanker, which had last carried a chemical solution and still held residue.
A pressure logger shows a brief negative dip in the area main at the time the plant pump tripped.
Samples in the area carry the same chemical signature as the tanker residue, strongest nearest the hydrant.
The contractor had no hydrant permit and no backflow protection on the fill connection.
After the area was flushed and the tanker filling stopped, samples cleared within a day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The chemical yard spilled into the street and the spill entered a broken main
The pressure dip siphoned tanker residue back through the submerged fill hose into the area main
The plant treated water picked up the chemical at the intake
Residents are copying each other complaints without a real taste

inference.explanation: A submerged hose in a residue holding tanker, a timed negative pressure dip, a matching chemical signature strongest at the hydrant, and clearance after flushing and stopping the filling all show backsiphonage at the hydrant connection. A spill into a broken main would need a break, and none was found; the plant source would affect the whole system.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Stop the unpermitted filling, require permitted hydrant use with backflow protection, and keep area sampling until results stay clean
Excavate around the chemical yard looking for a broken main
Raise the plant treatment chemical dose to mask the taste

nextClue.explanation: Permitted, protected hydrant filling removes the siphon path, and continued sampling verifies the area water stays clean.

clueText.nc-a: Area samples stay clean for a week and permitted filling with protection begins without incident.
clueText.nc-b: No break was found and the pattern followed the tanker connection, not the yard ground.
clueText.nc-c: Masking a taste does not remove a contaminant or its entry path.

tasks.prompt: A reduced pressure backflow preventer at an Ontario arena floods its pit with discharged water every few days, and the arena manager thinks the town pressure is at fault.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reduced pressure assembly on the arena service, due for its annual test. Pit discharge volumes are estimated from the pit pump log.

evidence.label: Town pressure at the arena is steady in the normal range, with no surges in the logger record.
The assembly relief port discharges in bursts even at steady pressure and steady arena demand.
A differential test shows the first check valve holding only a fraction of its required pressure difference.
Debris, a scale chip, is found on the first check seat when the assembly is opened.
After cleaning and a repair kit, the assembly passes its full test and the pit stays dry.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Town pressure surges are forcing the relief port open
The fouled first check cannot hold its differential, so the relief port discharges as it is designed to do
The pit is filling with groundwater
The arena is back pressuring the assembly with its Zamboni fill pump

inference.explanation: Steady town pressure, discharge at steady conditions, a failed differential on the first check, a scale chip on its seat, and a passing test after repair all show the assembly was doing its job against a fouled check. Groundwater would not follow test results, and arena backpressure would show in demand patterns.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Record the passed test, set the next annual test date, and add relief discharge checks to the arena service visits
Plug the relief port to keep the pit dry
Ask the town to lower its pressure for the arena

nextClue.explanation: Dated retesting keeps the assembly protective, and discharge checks catch fouling before the pit floods again.

clueText.nc-a: The pit stays dry and the assembly passes its next scheduled test on time.
clueText.nc-b: Plugging the relief port would defeat the protection the assembly provides.
clueText.nc-c: Town pressure was steady and normal throughout.

tasks.prompt: A musty taste fills one Ontario tank zone each late summer, while the rest of the system tastes fine and all safety results pass.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone fed by one elevated tank. The tank interior was last inspected six years ago.

evidence.label: Complaints map exactly to the tank zone boundary and stop at the zone valves.
Plant treated water and other zones show no musty taste in the same weeks.
Tank inspection finds a slime layer and sediment across the tank floor, with a musty odour inside the tank itself.
Residual in the tank runs lower than the plant by 0.4 mg/L through the warm weeks.
After the tank is cleaned and returned to service, the musty taste clears from the zone within a week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The source water has a seasonal algae taste affecting the whole system
Growth and sediment inside this tank are producing the musty taste for its zone only
Zone residents are influenced by each other reports
The plant carbon feed has stopped working

inference.explanation: A zone boundary pattern, clean plant and other zone water, slime and sediment with the same odour inside the tank, and clearance after cleaning all place the taste source in the tank. A source or plant cause would cross the zone valves into other areas.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Set the tank on a regular interior inspection and cleaning cycle and trend zone taste complaints each summer
Add carbon feed at the plant for the whole system
Flush the zone mains every week each summer

nextClue.explanation: A cleaning cycle prevents the build up returning, and complaint trending verifies summers stay clear.

clueText.nc-a: The next two summers pass with no musty complaints from the zone under the cleaning cycle.
clueText.nc-b: Plant water was clean throughout; the tank was the source.
clueText.nc-c: Flushing cannot remove slime growing inside the tank.

tasks.prompt: Homes close to an Ontario plant complain of strong chlorine taste, while the plant says it must keep its dose up for the far end of the system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional system with a long distribution reach. Residual is sampled by distance from the plant on the same day.

evidence.label: Near plant samples read 1.7 mg/L, mid system 1.0 mg/L, and far end 0.5 mg/L on the same day.
The plant dose was raised last year to rescue far end residuals that had been failing.
Far end water age is about four days, driven by an oversized storage tank cycling shallowly.
Near plant complaints began within weeks of the dose increase.
A trial deepening tank cycling raises far end residual to 0.7 mg/L at the same plant dose.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Near plant homes have become sensitive to normal chlorine levels
The dose needed at the far end is set by water age, so near plant water carries more chlorine than it needs
The plant analyzer over reads and the dose is actually low
Near plant pipes are adding chlorine taste of their own

inference.explanation: A smooth residual gradient by distance, complaints starting with the dose raise, far end age driven by shallow tank cycling, and far end recovery from cycling alone all show the dose is compensating for age. The analyzer is confirmed by the matching field samples, and pipes do not add chlorine.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Deepen tank cycling permanently and review whether the plant dose can step back down while far end trending continues
Tell near plant homes the taste is unavoidable forever
Install point of use filters at plant expense for near plant homes

nextClue.explanation: Fixing the age driver lets the dose come down for everyone, and far end trending guards the reason the dose was raised.

clueText.nc-a: Far end residual holds at 0.65 mg/L and the plant dose steps down, with near plant complaints ending.
clueText.nc-b: The trial showed the age driver could be fixed, so the taste was not unavoidable.
clueText.nc-c: Filters treat one symptom while the system dose stays higher than needed.

tasks.prompt: A rotten egg odour comes from both hot and cold taps at homes on one Ontario dead end street, worst after quiet weekends, and the water is otherwise safe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional dead end street with low use. Samples are checked for sulphide and the hydrant flush water is inspected.

evidence.label: The odour is strongest in first draw water and clears after a few minutes of running.
Flushing the dead end brings up black, slimy water at first, then clear water with no odour.
Sulphide is detected in the first flush water and not in the through main feeding the street.
Residual at the dead end is near zero on Monday mornings and normal after flushing.
Homes on the through main report no odour at any time.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The plant water contains sulphide from its source
Anaerobic growth in the stagnant dead end is producing sulphide and black slime between uses
Each home water heater is producing the odour
A sewer cross connection is leaking gas into the water lines

inference.explanation: Odour in cold as well as hot water rules out heaters, the through main is clean, and black slime with sulphide appears only in the dead end flush water, with residual gone after stagnation. That is anaerobic growth in the dead end itself. A sewer gas path would not produce slime in the flush water or follow flushing so exactly.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Put the dead end on a scheduled flushing program and trend its Monday residual and odour reports
Advise each home to replace its water heater anode
Raise the plant dose for the whole system

nextClue.explanation: Scheduled flushing removes the stagnant growth conditions, and Monday trending verifies the odour stays away.

clueText.nc-a: Monday residuals hold above 0.3 mg/L and no odour reports arrive for the next two months.
clueText.nc-b: Cold taps had the odour too, so heaters were not the source.
clueText.nc-c: The through main already carries normal residual at the current dose.

tasks.prompt: A petroleum taste affects three Ontario homes on one side of a street, starting weeks after a fuel spill at the corner gas station, and the street main samples are clean.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional homes with plastic service lines on the spill side of the street; homes opposite have copper services. Soil work from the spill cleanup is documented.

evidence.label: Affected homes all have polyethylene service lines running through the spill affected soil.
Homes across the street with copper services, on the same main, report no taste.
Street main samples at the hydrant are clean, while samples inside the affected homes carry the petroleum note.
The taste is strongest after the water sits in the service line overnight.
Replacing one home service line with a protected material ends the taste at that home within days.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The street main is contaminated with fuel along its length
Fuel in the soil is permeating the plastic service lines and entering the water as it sits in them
The gas station is connected to the water main by mistake
The three homes share a faulty plumbing vent

inference.explanation: Clean main samples, taste only in plastic serviced homes on the spill side, copper serviced neighbours unaffected, overnight strengthening, and a cure by service replacement all show permeation through the plastic services. A contaminated main would appear at the hydrant and at every home.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Program replacement of the remaining plastic services in the spill soil and keep sampling the affected homes until they clear
Flush the street main daily
Raise the system chlorine to burn off the taste

nextClue.explanation: Replacing the permeable services in the affected soil removes the entry path, and sampling verifies each home clears.

clueText.nc-a: Both remaining homes clear within days of their service replacements and stay clear.
clueText.nc-b: The main samples were already clean, so flushing cannot fix the services.
clueText.nc-c: Chlorine does not stop fuel permeating a plastic pipe wall.

tasks.prompt: A chloraminated Ontario system watches one neighbourhood lose total chlorine each August, with a faint ammonia smell at times, while plant chloramine formation is verified correct.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional chloramine system. The neighbourhood is the oldest water in the system, beyond two storage tanks in series.

evidence.label: Neighbourhood total chlorine falls from 1.6 to 0.5 mg/L through August while nitrite climbs and free ammonia falls.
Alkalinity and pH in the neighbourhood dip slightly as nitrite rises.
Water temperature there reaches 26 C and its age is estimated at eight days in summer.
Younger areas of the system hold total chlorine near plant values all summer.
A program of tank turnover improvement plus targeted flushing holds the neighbourhood total chlorine above 1.1 mg/L the next August, with nitrite near zero.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The plant is forming chloramine incorrectly each August
Nitrification in the warm, eight day old water is consuming chloramine and ammonia and releasing nitrite
The neighbourhood mains are leaking chloramine selectively
August sunlight is breaking down chloramine in the buried mains

inference.explanation: Ammonia falling, nitrite rising, pH and alkalinity dipping, confinement to the oldest warm water, correct plant formation, and control by turnover and flushing all show nitrification. Buried mains see no sunlight, and a leak cannot selectively remove chloramine while generating nitrite.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Keep the turnover and flushing program each summer and trend nitrite monthly in the neighbourhood from June
Add extra ammonia at the plant each August
Switch the neighbourhood to a separate free chlorine feed

nextClue.explanation: Monthly nitrite trending from June catches the next nitrification early, while turnover control keeps water age down.

clueText.nc-a: Nitrite stays near zero the following summer and total chlorine holds above 1.1 mg/L in August.
clueText.nc-b: Extra ammonia is the food source for the nitrifying bacteria.
clueText.nc-c: A separate feed is a major change the turnover results show is not needed.

tasks.prompt: Homes beyond a river bridge in an Ontario town lose water in every severe cold snap, while homes before the bridge never do, and the main crosses the river on the bridge deck.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional bridge crossing where the main runs in an insulated trough on the deck. Services beyond the bridge are standard depth.

evidence.label: Loss of water begins on the coldest nights and affects only the homes fed across the bridge.
The bridge trough insulation is found damaged and waterlogged on one section, exposing the main to deck air temperatures.
A temperature logger in the trough falls to minus 12 C while buried main temperatures stay above 0 C.
Letting a small bleed flow run through the crossing on the coldest nights keeps the beyond bridge homes in water.
After the trough insulation is replaced and sealed, the next cold snap passes with no losses beyond the bridge.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The beyond bridge services are all buried too shallow
The exposed bridge crossing main freezes at its damaged insulation section and cuts off everything beyond it
The town pumps cannot push water across the bridge in cold weather
Ice in the river is crushing the crossing main

inference.explanation: Only beyond bridge homes affected, a trough temperature of minus 12 C at damaged waterlogged insulation, protection from a bleed flow, and a clean cold snap after insulation repair all show the crossing main freezing. Shallow services would freeze one home at a time, not a whole area at once, and the crossing is on the deck, not in the river.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Add trough insulation checks to the autumn bridge inspection and keep the cold night bleed procedure as a backup
Bury the beyond bridge services deeper
Raise system pressure on cold nights

nextClue.explanation: Autumn insulation checks catch damage before freeze season, and the bleed backup protects the crossing if damage recurs.

clueText.nc-a: The crossing passes the next winter with insulation verified intact in autumn.
clueText.nc-b: The services thawed whenever the crossing flowed, so their depth was not the fault.
clueText.nc-c: Pressure does not prevent water in an exposed main from freezing.
